title: Variability-Matrix Scenario
description: One scenario in the audit variability matrix (5 payers x 5 specialties x 14 E/M codes x 3 num_problems x 3 MDM tiers x 3 difficulty tiers). Defines the input fields (chief complaint, patient demographics, history items) the Auditor Agent consumes, the metadata that drives the sampling / coverage matrix, and the expected-output fields the Grader scores against. Consumed by t_43ff3e89 (sampling strategy), t_785d35c1 (v1 sample set of 100), t_221a3d69 (rubric / ground truth), and the Auditor + Grader runtime in src/ai_billing_audit/.

scenario_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'sc_<short-descriptor>'. Used as the primary key across the sample manifest, the coverage report, and the rubric's gold set.

metadata.description: The six variability-matrix axes. Every combination of these axes is a unique cell in the 9,450-combination space; the sampler in t_43ff3e89 picks 100 of them.

payer.description: Insurance payer. Drives payer-specific E/M rule lookups (e.g. Medicare's split/shared visit policy vs. commercial payer rules).

specialty.description: Clinical specialty of the rendering provider. Drives the typical code distribution (e.g. cardiology leans toward 93000 ECG + E/M).

em_code.description: E/M CPT code being billed. Office/outpatient (99202-99215), initial inpatient (99221-99223), subsequent inpatient (99231-99233), and discharge (99238-99239) are all valid; the 9,450-cell count uses 99202-99215 only.

num_problems.description: Number of distinct problems addressed at the encounter (1 = single problem, 2 = dual problem, 3 = multi problem). Drives MDM complexity per the 2021 E/M guidelines.

mdm_tier.description: Medical Decision Making tier that the documented encounter supports. Must be consistent with num_problems and risk per the 2021 E/M MDM table; the rubric in t_221a3d69 flags mismatches.

difficulty.description: Difficulty tier for the Auditor. 'easy' = single problem, no Rx, no modifier flags. 'medium' = dual problem with Rx drug management. 'hard' = chronic + acute with surgery + global period + modifier-25 trap.

input.description: Everything the Auditor Agent sees. Mirrors the shape of a real chart note minus the billing lines (those are in expected_output for grading).

chief_complaint.description: The patient's stated reason for the visit, in 1-2 sentences. Always populated; never an empty string.

patient.description: Demographics relevant to coding. Age and sex are the only required fields; chronic conditions and allergies are optional context.

age.description: Age in years at the time of the encounter.

sex.description: Sex on file: M (male), F (female), O (other / not specified).

chronic_conditions.description: Optional list of chronic-condition labels (free text, e.g. 'Type 2 diabetes', 'CKD stage 3'). Not validated against ICD-10; provided for narrative realism.

history_items.description: Bulleted HPI / ROS / PFSH items the provider documented. At least one item is required; in practice easy scenarios have 2-4, medium 4-7, hard 6-12.

category.description: Which history block the item belongs to. HPI = history of present illness, ROS = review of systems, PFSH = past family / social history.

text.description: The verbatim line as it would appear in the chart.

vitals.description: Optional vitals block. Free-form key/value pairs (e.g. {'bp': '142/88', 'hr': 78}). Not constrained; the rubric does not score vitals values.

expected_output.description: The ground truth the Grader scores the Auditor's output against. Always includes at least one diagnosis code, at least one CPT line, and a one-paragraph MDM rationale that justifies the level.

code.description: ICD-10-CM code, e.g. 'E11.9' (type 2 diabetes uncomplicated), 'I10' (essential hypertension), 'K40.90' (unilateral inguinal hernia).

description.description: Human-readable label for the code. Used in the gold-set rubric (t_221a3d69) and the grader's TP/FP matching.

is_primary.description: True for the diagnosis that drives the E/M level. Exactly one code should be marked primary; the rubric fails the scenario if zero or more than one is primary.

diagnosis_codes.description: List of ICD-10-CM codes the encounter supports, in billing order. First entry is conventionally (but not required to be) the primary diagnosis.

mdm_rationale.description: One-paragraph natural-language justification for the MDM tier. Should explicitly mention (a) the number of problems addressed, (b) the data reviewed (labs, imaging, records), and (c) the risk of complications and/or morbidity. The rubric checks that each of those three axes is named.

code.description: CPT/HCPCS code. 5 digits, or 5 alphanumeric characters for Category II/III / HCPCS.

modifier.description: Optional CPT modifier (e.g. '25' for separately identifiable E/M on the same day as a procedure with a global period). The rubric requires modifier-25 on the E/M line for any scenario with surgery_with_global_period=true; absence is a hard flag.

rationale.description: Why this CPT applies. For E/M: the MDM tier and history items that justify the level. For procedures: the diagnosis that supports medical necessity.

code_selection.description: CPT/HCPCS lines the encounter should bill. The E/M line (99202-99215 / 99221-99239) is always present; additional procedure lines are present for hard scenarios (surgery, joint injection, etc.).

surgery_with_global_period.description: True if the encounter involves a procedure with a CMS global period (10/90-day). When true, the rubric enforces modifier-25 on the E/M line.
